advances: Obstructs only the fixed-weight selector using the full middle fiber and a mass-$aV$ dominated portion of the large endpoint. The identical body has a sharp-target point from a different, truncated subbody by the accepted predecessor.

proof:
Use the body and exact volume calculation in 81f1c1cb0440d242, with its $Q=q$, $r=2-q$, $C_+=C$ and $\lambda_1=x_1$. In particular $200/101<q<2$ and $(A+C)/2=L\subseteq B$. The lifted hull has projection $[-1,1]$, its extreme fibers are unchanged, and every contribution to the middle from the endpoints uses equal endpoint weights and lies in $L$. Thus its three fibers and mixed mass are the claimed ones. The masses $aV,V,V$ are all smaller than $(1+a/2)V$ because $0<a<10^{-8}$.

All first coordinates on $A$ are at least $(2-q)\alpha$, and all those on $C$ are at least $q\alpha$. The simplex centroid's first coordinate is $1/5$. Hence every selected $y_\sigma$ has first coordinate at least $h$, even for fractional $\sigma$. In fact
$$
h=\frac15-\frac{3a}{50(1+2a)}>\beta,
$$
since $1/5-\beta=10^{-6}$ and $3a/[50(1+2a)]<6\cdot10^{-10}$. At each endpoint base the maximum of $x_1+(1-q)\beta z$ is $\beta$: the two maxima are $(2-q)\beta-(1-q)\beta$ and $q\beta+(1-q)\beta$. Thus the cap misses both endpoint fibers completely. On $B$ the cap $x_1\ge h$ is a copy of $B$ with linear scale $1-h$ about its vertex with first coordinate one. Its mixed mass is
$$
\mu(H)=V(1-h)^4=\Gamma_4 V\left(1+\frac{3a}{40(1+2a)}\right)^4.
$$
For $0<a\le1$, the mean-value theorem bounds the parenthesized fourth power minus one by $(3a/10)(43/40)^3=(238521/640000)a<a/2$. This gives $\mu(H)<\Gamma_4(1+a/2)V=(\Gamma_4/2)W$ for the same cap at every selected point.
statement:
Let $B$ be the standard $4$-simplex of volume $V$, $\alpha=17/100$, $\beta=199999/1000000$, $L=B\cap\{\alpha\le x_1\le\beta\}$, $m=|L|/V=(83/100)^4-(800001/1000000)^4$, $q=m^{-1/4}$, $A=(2-q)L$, $C=qL$, and $a=(2m^{1/4}-1)^4$. The lifted convex hull at bases $-1,0,1$ has the actual fibers $A,B,C$, of volumes $aV,V,V$ with $0<a<10^{-8}$. Each is strictly below half the original mixed mass $W=(2+a)V$. For every $0\le\sigma\le\mathbf 1_C dx$ of mass $aV$, put
$$
y_\sigma=\frac{Vg_B+aVg_A+\int x\,d\sigma}{V(1+2a)},\qquad h=\frac{1/5+2a\alpha}{1+2a}.
$$
The single closed ambient cap $H=\{x_1+(1-q)\beta z\ge h\}$ contains all $(0,y_\sigma)$ and has raw mass strictly below $(\Gamma_4/2)W$, where $\Gamma_4=(4/5)^4$. In particular the maximum normalized depth of the prescribed selector is strictly below $\Gamma_4/2$.
title: A four-dimensional slab obstruction to the fixed-weight endpoint selector
